headline: Federal judge dismisses DOJ lawsuit seeking Vermont voter rolls
dek: The ruling rejects the federal government’s demand for a complete, unredacted voter list, Vermont officials said, including sensitive personal information.
body: U.S. District Judge Mary Kay Lanthier dismissed the Department of Justice’s lawsuit seeking Vermont’s voter rolls on Sept. 17, according to the Vermont Attorney General’s Office.

The case centered on the federal government’s demand for a complete, unredacted copy of the state’s voter list. Vermont’s attorney general said the court agreed that Title III of the Civil Rights Act of 1960 did not authorize that demand and that the request lacked a factual basis or lawful purpose.

Vermont Secretary of State Sarah Copeland Hanzas and Attorney General Charity Clark said the information sought could include voters’ home addresses, dates of birth, Social Security numbers and driver’s license numbers. They praised the decision as a protection for the privacy of Vermont voters.

The dismissal leaves Vermont’s refusal to provide the records intact under the demand challenged in the case. The attorney general’s office described the ruling as a response to the federal request for the state’s full voter list.
author: NorthEast News Desk
